plan: Full experiment-design document delivered (sections A–J in order, plus the §F test matrix). Key contents: (A) target capability quoted verbatim; (B) I/O contract list[str]->str, three pseudocode signatures, three invariants on the returned string; (C) rationale for each binding decision D1–D7 with worked examples (casefold vs lower via 'Straße', NFC via composed/decomposed 'café', tie-break via 'Apple'/'apple' codepoints); (D) pseudocode for tokenize, sort_words, _sort_locale (save/restore setlocale), with rejection of internal whitespace; (E) baseline/positive/negative controls including no-mutation and AsciiEquivalence; (F) 13-row test matrix covering empty list, single word, duplicates, mixed-case ASCII, NFC/NFD pair, apostrophe token, leading/trailing whitespace, internal-whitespace rejection (negative), n=1000 random, three-way case-twins, default≡locale equivalence, and locale divergence on 'über'; (G) analysis plan with paper-only footnote on GNU sort and wall-clock; (H) three-tier feasibility table (stdlib offline / sandbox execution / paper-only); (I) six limitations including locale-process-globality and NFC-not-homographs; (J) module skeleton word_sort.py with tokenize, sort_words, _sort_locale and __main__ print boundary that adds exactly one newline. No execution or measurement is claimed.
